# Backtest on real data (1946-2025), cutoffs 1960-2014

<!-- Generated by `python -m forecast.backtest --out docs/backtests/2026-10-markov-baseline.md` on 2026-10-18. -->

**Data:** V-Dem v16 (electoral democracy index) and UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict 26.1, as imported by `tools/importers/`.
**States:** civil war (intrastate conflict of 1,000+ battle deaths), armed conflict (any state-based conflict on the territory), democracy (V-Dem polyarchy ≥ 0.5), autocracy. Coups are left out until the Powell & Thyne licence is resolved.
**Method:** for each cutoff year X from 1960 to 2014, train on transitions before X, start from each country's state in X−1, and score forecasts for X and X+4.

**Caveats:**
- V-Dem scores for past years were coded later by experts who knew what happened next, so this is kinder than a true real-time test. Older V-Dem versions (v1 was 2016) would allow a stricter one.
- The states are coarse and the thresholds are a first guess. Results are a baseline to beat, not a forecast anyone should act on.

Lower is better. A model is only useful if it beats both baselines.

## 1 year ahead

| model | forecasts | Brier | log score |
|---|---|---|---|
| markov | 8997 | 0.1661 | 0.3621 |
| persistence | 8997 | 0.1830 | 0.4405 |
| base-rate | 8997 | 0.6406 | 1.1365 |

## Calibration of the Markov model, 1 year ahead

When the model said about p, how often did it happen?

- **civil-war:** said 1% → happened 1% (n=8581), said 71% → happened 70% (n=416)
- **armed-conflict:** said 3% → happened 4% (n=7847), said 22% → happened 30% (n=77), said 68% → happened 69% (n=1073)
- **democracy:** said 1% → happened 2% (n=6098), said 97% → happened 97% (n=2899)
- **autocracy:** said 4% → happened 3% (n=3664), said 23% → happened 18% (n=724), said 95% → happened 93% (n=4609)
